They help build and run the systems behind the intelligence pipeline, including AI-assisted workflows with verification and monitoring. Internships.overview:
[About the Role] CrowdStrike seeks the best intelligence analysts, threat responders, researchers and engineers to help it maintain and advance its position as market leader in cloud-delivered next-generation endpoint protection. It combines intellectual curiosity with proven and nascent technologies to deliver actionable intelligence that stays ahead of adversaries and provides breach detection and prevention.
[Intel Automation Team] Collecting, processing and exploring information at large scale is at the core of the Intelligence mission. The Intelligence Automation team prototypes, builds and operates the systems that make up the Intelligence pipeline. Its work spans data science and machine learning, platform and infrastructure engineering, traditional software engineering and security research. One theme is constant: AI is used to build systems that do real work reliably, meaning designing the tools, environments, guardrails and evaluations that let AI-driven workflows be trusted with production tasks. The team is globally distributed and connects mostly via Slack and Zoom, so working unsupervised, communicating asynchronously and taking initiative to maintain lines of communication is crucial.
Internships.responsibilities:
[What You'll Do] Choose your own project based on your preferences and experience, across areas such as:
- Data Science and AI: multi-agent orchestration, RAG, sandboxing, software factory, evaluations, self-improvement loops
- Infrastructure and Platform Engineering: operating containerized workloads and CI/CD pipelines, and building the environments and tooling that development and AI workflows run in safely
- Software Engineering: writing scalable, production-ready code and the tests and automation that keep it correct
- Security Research: binary analysis, vulnerability research and threat intelligence
Regardless of project you will:
- Architect AI-assisted systems with real-world impact: define how AI components integrate with tools, data sources and each other, and how their output is verified
- Learn what it takes to run AI workflows in production: evaluation, monitoring, failure handling and continuous improvement
- Work directly with Senior Data Scientists, Engineers and Researchers
Internships.requirements:
[What You'll Need]
- Undergraduate/Masters student in your penultimate year of study (2028 graduate) in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics or a related field
- Solid knowledge and experience in at least one of: Python, Go, Rust, JavaScript/TypeScript
- Comfortable working in a Linux environment, with git and modern CI/CD
- Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes; you can show repos, workflows or projects where you directed AI agents to do substantial work
- Ability to design around AI rather than just prompt it: you naturally think in interfaces, test suites, failure modes and quality gates when letting an AI system act on real tasks
- Ability to communicate technical detail in a simple, top-down manner
- Ability to independently make sound, justifiable decisions and take action
- Ability to plan, organise and prioritise work independently and meet deadlines

- A problem solver with a can-do attitude who loves interesting challenges
- Interested in the latest technologies in your field of expertise
- Self-motivated and actively seeking opportunities to grow

Internships.job_description_summary: The intern works on a defined research project at the intersection of AI, cybersecurity and computer systems at Horizon3 (autonomous pentesting). They read papers, build prototypes, run experiments, and work with security data such as attack paths, telemetry and cloud environments alongside researchers and attack engineers. The posting asks for a CS or related student with strong fundamentals and interest in systems security or machine learning.
Internships.overview:
[Get to Know Us] Horizon3.ai is a fast-growing, remote cybersecurity company whose mission is to enable organizations to proactively find, fix and verify exploitable attack vectors before criminals exploit them. Its flagship NodeZero platform delivers production-safe autonomous pentests and other assessment operations that scale across the largest internal, external, cloud and hybrid cloud environments. NodeZero is used by organizations from small educational institutions to government agencies and Global 100 enterprises, by IT Ops/SecOps teams, consulting pentesters, and MSSPs and MSPs. The team is a fusion of former U.S. Special Operations cyber operators, startup engineers and operators, and formerly frustrated cybersecurity practitioners, committed to solving ineffective security tools and false positives (alert fatigue), blind spots, 'checkbox' security culture, the cybersecurity skills shortage, and the long lead time and expense of outside consultants; a team of 'learn it alls' with a culture of respect, collaboration, ownership and results.
[An Overview] Horizon3 is looking for Research Interns to join Horizon3 AI Research and work on technical problems at the intersection of super intelligence, systems security and agentic systems for security. Interns work on a concrete research problem with researchers and engineers; depending on the project this may include AI agents for security, autonomous pentesting, attack-path reasoning, cyber deception, AI safety and security, security evaluation of AI systems, or new methods for reasoning over security data and environments. It is a hands-on research internship: study the problem and the literature, but also build, experiment, analyze results and communicate what you learn. Projects may involve research prototypes, experimental infrastructure, AI models or agents, security test environments, attack graphs, system telemetry or other technical artifacts. Interns are not expected to arrive with expertise in both AI and systems security; the company wants strong computer science foundations, meaningful experience in at least one relevant technical area and genuine interest in developing expertise across AI and security. Interns receive mentorship and technical guidance, but are also expected to show curiosity, initiative and willingness to investigate difficult technical questions independently.
Internships.responsibilities:
[What You'll Do]
- Work on a defined research project at the intersection of AI, cybersecurity and computer systems
- Understand the research problem, relevant technical background and existing approaches
- Read and critically evaluate academic papers and technical material related to the project
- Develop and implement research ideas, algorithms, prototypes or experimental systems
- Design and run experiments to evaluate research hypotheses and technical approaches
- Analyze experimental results carefully and identify limitations, failure modes and unexpected behavior
- Work with security data and environments that may include attack paths, graphs, telemetry, configurations, identities, networks, cloud systems or security controls
- Collaborate with Horizon3 researchers, security engineers, attack engineers and other technical teams as appropriate for the project
- Document methods, experiments and findings clearly so the work can be reproduced and continued after the internship
- Present research progress during the internship and communicate final findings to the broader team
- Contribute, when appropriate, to research outputs such as technical reports, prototypes, open-source artifacts, patent disclosures or academic publications
Internships.requirements:
[What You'll Bring]
- Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science or a related technical field, or equivalent technical experience
- Strong computer science fundamentals and programming ability
- Experience or demonstrated interest in systems security, super intelligence / machine learning, computer systems or a closely related area
- Ability to translate technical ideas into working implementations
- Ability to read technical material and learn unfamiliar concepts independently
- Curiosity about difficult technical problems and willingness to investigate why a system behaves the way it does
- Interest in both research and engineering (you may be stronger in one, but should be comfortable with both ideas and implementations)
- Ability to receive technical feedback, revise your approach and learn from mentors and collaborators
- Ability to communicate technical work clearly in writing and discussion
Internships.preferred:
[What Sets You Apart]
- Experience conducting research through an academic research group, independent project, thesis, capstone, internship or comparable technical work
- Experience in systems security, offensive security, defensive security, penetration testing, vulnerability research, operating systems, networks, cloud security, identity systems or related areas
- Experience with machine learning, deep learning, large language models, AI agents, reinforcement learning, planning, search, graph algorithms or related AI methods
- Experience building research prototypes, experimental systems, benchmarks, test environments or evaluation frameworks
- Familiarity with security concepts such as attack paths, Active Directory, cloud environments, identity systems, security controls, adversarial techniques or autonomous security systems
- Experience reading and implementing ideas from academic papers
- Participation in research, security competitions, CTFs, open-source projects or other technically substantial extracurricular work
- Research publications, conference presentations, open-source contributions or other evidence of strong technical work (publications are valuable but not required)
Exceptional undergraduate students with strong technical or research experience are encouraged to apply; PhD students whose research interests align with Horizon3 AI Research are also strongly encouraged to apply. Each intern is paired with a research mentor and assigned a concrete research problem with clear technical objectives; the exact project depends on the intern's background, interests and the Lab's active research directions.

The 2027 CSI program runs during the summer with start dates between May 17, 2027 and June 21, 2027 and flexible end dates through September 24, 2027. CSI lets selected candidates apply their skills to projects in areas of national importance such as critical infrastructure risk analysis and security, energy infrastructure modernization and resilience, and defense critical infrastructure. The program includes professional and technical development activities with lab Subject Matter Experts, networking with fellow interns and lab employees, and learning about the breadth of LLNL's support to US national security.

- Demonstrated effective communication skills
- Ability to present and communicate concepts and ideas
- Experience applying engineering principles to solve technical problems
- Ability to work in a team environment
- Demonstrated exposure through coursework or relevant experience to one or more of: machine learning and super intelligence; risk and/or decision analysis; infrastructure modeling and/or simulation; threat and/or hazard modeling; data analysis; open-source research and analysis; systems engineering; system decomposition; operations research and/or optimization

Internships.job_description_summary: The intern joins Zoox's Quantitative Risk Assessment team within System Design & Mission Assurance, applying statistical and machine learning methods to quantify safety and risk of autonomous driving systems using fleet and simulation data. Work includes modeling rare safety events and analyzing large datasets with SQL, Python or Spark. Candidates need strong statistics, ML and SQL/Python fundamentals and must relocate to the Bay Area for a 12-week internship.
Internships.overview:
[About Our Internship Program] Zoox's internship program offers hands-on experience with cutting-edge technology, mentorship from some of the industry's brightest minds and the chance to contribute to real projects. It seeks interns with strong academic performance, engagement beyond the classroom, intellectual curiosity and a genuine interest in Zoox's mission to create autonomous mobility from the ground up.
[Job Description] As an intern in the Quantitative Risk Assessment (QRA) team within System Design & Mission Assurance, you apply rigorous statistical methods and machine learning techniques to quantify safety and risk across autonomous driving systems. You work with complex real-world fleet and simulation datasets to model rare safety events, establish statistical baselines and develop metrics that validate the safety and mission assurance of the purpose-built robotaxi.
Internships.responsibilities:
[In this Role, You Will...]
- Formulate and build statistical and machine learning models to evaluate system performance and analyze rare, high-consequence safety events
- Process and analyze large-scale datasets using SQL, Python or distributed data frameworks (Spark/Databricks) to extract actionable insights on vehicle behavior and operational risk
- Apply advanced statistical methods (e.g., Poisson processes, GLMs, Bayesian inference, point process models or spatial-temporal modeling) to evaluate safety-critical metrics
- Collaborate with systems engineers and safety leads to translate complex quantitative models into rigorous mission assurance decisions
Internships.requirements:
[Internship Requirements]
- Currently pursuing a Master's or Ph.D. in Statistics, Data Science, Machine Learning, Computer Science or a related quantitative engineering/scientific discipline
- Enrolled in good academic standing at an accredited college or university throughout the internship
- Expected to graduate between Fall 2027 and Summer 2028
- Able to commit to a full-time, 12-week internship beginning in May/June 2027
- Ability to relocate to the Bay Area, California for the duration of the internship
- Interns may not use proprietary information they work on for a thesis or published work with their university, or distribute it to anyone outside Zoox
[Qualifications]
- Statistical Foundations: deep understanding of probability theory, regression, Generalized Linear Models (GLMs), hypothesis testing and Bayesian methods; experience or coursework in spatial statistics, space-time models, point process models or causal inference
- Machine Learning & Modeling: strong fundamentals in statistical modeling and ML (supervised and unsupervised learning, model validation, metric evaluation)
- Data Manipulation & Querying: proficiency with basic-to-intermediate SQL and Python for data querying, cleaning and statistical modeling (or alternative packages such as Spark, dplyr or R)
- Communication & Problem Solving: ability to break down ambiguous operational or system questions into structured statistical problems and clearly communicate complex quantitative findings to technical stakeholders
Internships.preferred:
[Bonus Qualifications]
- Large-Scale Data Processing: experience querying, pipeline-building and modeling massive datasets using Spark, Databricks or cloud platforms
- Rare-Event Modeling & Domain Experience: familiarity with autonomous vehicles, transportation network companies (TNCs), quantitative safety/risk modeling, or fraud/rare-event detection
- AI-Assisted Workflow & Tooling: experience using AI-assisted data analysis, modern coding agents or LLM-driven research workflows to accelerate data exploration and model development

[About Nexus] 'You don't have an AI story if you don't have your data story.' NexusOne is the converged data platform for the AI era: composable by design, built on an open-source foundation and AI-native from the ground up, with one identity, one governance envelope and one operational layer across every mainframe, data lake, warehouse and streaming system, so enterprises bring their existing stack along instead of rebuilding it while still giving AI agents full context across the estate. Principles: sovereign data, interoperable systems, decoupled intelligence, delivered the way modern software should be; no rip-and-replace, no multi-year transformation. CEO Anu Jain describes turning the 'ball of yarn' of data integrations into a unified engine. 85+ open-source tools pre-integrated; AI-native automations that deploy and self-heal the stack; forward-deployed engineers building with customer teams. It is tripling revenue year over year, backed by Insight Partners, running in production in difficult environments: credit risk data for 90%+ of US small businesses (40M+) every month; intent signals for 300M+ subscribers monthly for Africa's largest telco; the data and AI layer for a Top 3 US bank. 100+ people across the US and India, headquartered in Atlanta; hires people who would rather ship the rocket than brief someone on it.
[THE OPPORTUNITY] Data Engineering Interns join the product and delivery team in Atlanta for Summer 2027, excited about where modern data engineering meets AI. 'This is not a shadowing internship': write real code, build real pipelines and contribute to features and integrations running in enterprise production, including agentic workflows that put data to work on its own. Interns are paired with senior engineers and solution architects, own a defined project for the summer and present it to the team at the end.

[WHAT YOU WILL DO]
- Help onboard enterprise customer workloads to NexusOne, including data ingestion, transformation, analytics and AI ops

- Contribute to agentic data workflows: pipelines and integrations that let AI agents act on enterprise data
- Work hands-on with modern data technologies including Kubernetes, Apache Spark, dbt, Trino, Airflow and Iceberg

Internships.job_description_summary: The intern works on real optical hardware in the lab, characterizing silicon photonics units on bench instrumentation, building measurement automation, and analyzing repeatability and drift. They deliver a recommendation that influences how Lightmatter's next products are tested. Candidates should be Bachelor's students in electrical engineering, physics or optical engineering with lab equipment experience and Python programming.
Internships.overview:
[About Lightmatter] Lightmatter is leading the revolution in AI data center infrastructure. It invented the world's first 3D-stacked photonics engine, Passage, capable of connecting thousands to millions of processors at the speed of light in extreme-scale data centers for advanced AI and HPC workloads. It raised $400 million in its Series D round at a $4.4 billion valuation and will keep accelerating data center photonics and growing every department. It invites people passionate about complex challenges, impact and expertise in their craft to join its scientists, engineers and industry leaders: '(re)inventing the future of computing with light.'
[About this job] The System Level Test team owns the final at-speed test of Lightmatter's silicon photonics products, high-speed optical interconnects that move data between the processors powering AI datacenters, where copper is running out of reach and light is taking over. The team builds the test methods, the automation and the data behind the pass vs fail decision. This summer's project is a hands-on optical characterization and correlation study to improve how products are tested in production: work on real optical hardware in the lab, build the measurement automation, generate the data and write the recommendation that decides whether the approach moves forward; the result directly influences how next products are tested.
Internships.responsibilities:
[Responsibilities]
- Characterize a set of silicon photonics units on bench optical instrumentation, measuring output power, modulation amplitude, extinction ratio and wavelength
- Build automation to run measurements, control the lab setup and log results in a consistent, reusable data format
- Correlate unit measurements against a calibrated laboratory reference and quantify per-unit offsets and population spread
- Measure unit stability across time, temperature and repeated re-insertion, and analyze repeatability and drift
- Deliver a feasibility and gap assessment with a clear recommendation, including the calibration and maintenance scheme needed for production deployment
Internships.requirements:
[Requirements]
- Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's program in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Optical Engineering or a related field
- Coursework or project experience in at least one of: integrated circuit design, device or circuit characterization, or electrical or optical testing
- Hands-on experience with standard lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, power supplies or optical power meters, from coursework, research or a prior internship
- Programming experience in Python or a similar language, including reading and plotting measurement data
[Export Control] Candidates should have the capacity to comply with the federally mandated requirements of U.S. export control laws.
Internships.preferred:
[Preferred Qualifications]
- Research, lab or prior internship experience in photonics or semiconductors
- Experience automating lab instruments (PyVISA, SCPI or similar)
- Familiarity with basic statistics: mean, standard deviation, repeatability, and gauge or measurement uncertainty
- Publications, projects or open-source contributions related to the role

The minimum qualifications ask for BS or MS students in electrical or computer engineering with experience or desire to develop automated bench measurements, bench test equipment familiarity, circuits knowledge, and entry-level programming.
Internships.overview:
[Intro] 'Are you a problem solver looking for a hands-on internship position with a market-leading company that will help develop your career and reward you intellectually and professionally?'
[About Analog Devices] ADI (NASDAQ: ADI) is a global semiconductor leader bridging the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge, combining analog, digital, AI and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and advance automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers; revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25. Interns learn from the brightest minds, work on meaningful projects alongside a team of experts and build a professional network in an environment of respect and responsibility. ADI's culture values aligned goals, work-life balance, continuous and life-long learning and shared rewards; the program features lunch-and-learn topics and social events, and ADI aims to develop interns so they are first considered for full-time roles.
[Product Engineer Intern] ADI seeks an ambitious ECE student as a Product (Design Evaluation) Engineer on the RTP IC development team (Summer 2027), joining a team of digital, analog and mixed-signal CMOS engineers and algorithm and software developers implementing state-of-the-art RF chips. As a member of the Product engineering team you are responsible for a specific product or group of products from product definition through production and release, participating in pre-silicon system development emulations and verification pre and post tape-out. There is a huge variety of possible tasks (software algorithm validation; digital, RF and analog evaluation, etc.), working with the full development team as the product moves from concept to customer.
Internships.responsibilities:
[Duties]
- Perform functional and performance testing of new system and core technologies
- Debug, evaluate, characterize and analyze integrated circuits across all operating conditions; document and present findings to the design team and the greater team
- Use precision measurement equipment such as high-speed scopes, spectrum and network analyzers to establish RF, analog, power and/or digital performance metrics
- Develop bench hardware and software to control and automate bench test equipment using Python and other programming languages
- Navigate design databases for products to develop test solutions and make recommendations on testability, manufacturability, qualification readiness and field quality
Internships.requirements:
[Minimum Qualifications]
- Enrolled in a BS or MS degree in EE or ECE (preferably a rising Senior or a candidate entering an MSEE program in Fall 2027)
- Experience or desire developing automated bench measurements
- Familiarity with bench test equipment including spectrum analyzers, oscilloscopes and signal generators
- Circuits knowledge including experience in an area related to analog circuits, RF circuits, signals and systems, ADCs, DACs, high-speed serial interfaces, microcontrollers
- Entry-level knowledge of a programming language such as LabVIEW, Python, Visual BASIC, HTML and/or C/C++
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
- Strong time management and team skills
- Clear, accurate and timely written and verbal communication
[Export licensing] For positions requiring access to technical data, ADI may have to obtain export licensing approval from the U.S. Department of Commerce (BIS) and/or the U.S. Department of State (DDTC); applicants other than US Citizens, US Permanent Residents and protected individuals under 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) may have to go through an export licensing review process.

Internships.job_description_summary: The intern at Entegris' Bloomington site contributes to embedded software for industrial and electromechanical products used in semiconductor manufacturing, working with microcontrollers, sensors, controllers and instrumentation. They gain hands-on experience in hardware and firmware integration, testing and troubleshooting while completing a defined summer project, final presentation and technical handoff. Candidates should be enrolled in computer engineering, electrical engineering, computer science or a related program; prior professional embedded experience is not required.
Internships.overview:
[Intro] Entegris uses advanced science to enable technologies that transform the world and seeks employees with the drive to continue the mission.
[The Role] The Bloomington, MN site seeks an Embedded Software Engineering Intern for the Summer 2027 season, a 12-14 week assignment. You contribute to embedded software for industrial and electromechanical products used in semiconductor manufacturing, working with microcontrollers, sensors, controllers and instrumentation. With guidance from an engineering mentor you gain hands-on experience in hardware and firmware integration, testing, troubleshooting and documentation while completing a defined summer project, final presentation and technical handoff.
Internships.responsibilities:
[What You'll Do]
- Develop, modify and test embedded C/C++ software for microcontrollers, sensors, controllers and instrumentation with guidance from an engineering mentor
- Integrate and verify interactions between hardware and firmware
- Assist with reproducing defects, collecting evidence, investigating root causes and documenting findings
- Create and run unit, integration and regression tests
- Write Python scripts for test automation, data collection and basic analysis
- Use Git for version control and participate in code reviews
- Prepare clear technical documentation, test records and change summaries
- Follow team practices for controlled software builds and releases
- Complete a defined summer project and present results, lessons learned and recommendations
- Provide an organized technical handoff so the team can continue or maintain the work
Internships.requirements:
[What We Seek]
- Foundational C or C++ programming experience from coursework, laboratory work, personal projects or student-team projects
- Basic understanding of microcontrollers, digital electronics and how software interacts with hardware, shown through coursework or projects
- Interest in embedded software, electronics, sensors, controls or instrumentation
- Ability to approach technical problems methodically, ask questions and learn from feedback
- Clear written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively
- Attention to detail when testing, documenting and managing code changes
- Previous professional embedded software experience is not required; academic, personal and student-team projects are welcome
[Desired Major(s)] Currently enrolled in a bachelor's or graduate degree program in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related field.
[Eligibility] Must be a currently enrolled student; available to work 40 hours a week, M-F (8a-5p) beginning in January through June (as written on the posting, although the role is described as Summer 2027); must be familiar with the university's co-op program requirements; Entegris is not hiring co-op/intern candidates who will need, now or in the future, sponsorship through the H1-B lottery; do not apply if you will need immigration sponsorship (e.g., H1B, TN, STEM OPT).

Projects.title: Python Security Log Analyzer
Projects.description: Build a command-line tool that parses simulated authentication logs (JSON lines), flags brute-force and password-spray patterns, and enriches suspicious IPs from a simulated threat-intel feed. Practiced in the style of a security analyst's investigation support work.
Projects.final_deliverable: A GitHub-ready repository with the analyzer script, simulated log generator, sample findings report, and README.

Projects.title: Mini SOAR Alert Triage Playbook
Projects.description: Build an automated triage workflow that pulls alerts as JSON from a mock REST API, enriches and scores them, and routes them to close, escalate or investigate, mirroring analyst automation work.
Projects.final_deliverable: A repository with the playbook code, mock alert API, test cases, and a short write-up of triage rules and accuracy.

Projects.title: Cloud Attack Path Mapper
Projects.description: Model a simulated cloud environment (identities, roles, network rules) as a graph, find attack paths to critical assets, and rank them by risk with suggested control fixes.
Projects.final_deliverable: A report and repository with the environment model, path-finding script, risk-ranked findings, and an attack path diagram.

Milestones.title: Explore and simulate the authentication data
Milestones.instructions: Write a script that generates about 5,000 simulated login events as JSON lines (timestamp, user, source_ip, result, method) including a few planted attacks: one brute-force burst, one password-spray, and one login from a rare IP. Load the file, count events by user, IP and result, and note what normal traffic looks like.
Milestones.deliverable: data/auth_logs.jsonl, generator script, and a short notes file listing baseline statistics
Milestones.resource_title: Python docs: json - JSON encoder and decoder

Milestones.title: Build the analyzer
Milestones.instructions: Create analyzer.py with a command-line interface that reads a log file and applies detection rules: N failed logins from one IP in a time window, one IP failing against many users, and success after many failures. Print findings as JSON. Run and test it on Linux or WSL.
Milestones.deliverable: analyzer.py with CLI flags and at least three detection rules
Milestones.resource_title: Python docs: argparse - Parser for command-line options

Milestones.title: Investigate the findings
Milestones.instructions: For each finding, build a short timeline, enrich the source IP against a simulated threat-intel list, and map the behavior to a known technique. Write a one-paragraph verdict and recommended response per finding.
Milestones.deliverable: findings_report.md with timelines, enrichment results, and recommended actions

Milestones.title: Publish a GitHub-ready deliverable
Milestones.instructions: Clean the code, add a README (purpose, install, usage, sample output, detection rules, limitations), add a .gitignore, make small descriptive commits, and push to a public repository.
Milestones.deliverable: Public GitHub repository link with README, code, sample data, and report
Milestones.resource_title: GitHub Docs: About the repository README file
